prize_parts.citation: for the optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms and its realisation at 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, confirmed in independent laboratories

statement.case_for: I keep B029 as the whole prize, and nothing in the first round moved me off it. Four of eight configurations contain it, and each of the four members who prefer something else still names it as a serious fallback; that is a count, not a proof, so I rest on the science. The achievement has three parts that I look for in a measurement prize. There is an original idea (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, which cancels the trapping light shift so that thousands of atoms are interrogated at once). There is a decisive realisation (Ye's group, taking systematic uncertainty and stability to the 10^-18 level, including the many-body regime). And there is independent confirmation, with JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB and SYRTE agreeing in frequency-ratio comparisons across continents. This is the patient calibration-and-systematics work that makes a result believable and durable. It already delivers physics about nature (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on drifting constants, dark-matter searches), so the redefinition of the second is a consequence we do not need to wait for. The chair's questions on credit are answered as far as the supplied record allows: the two-name set matches the proposal and the realisation, and no member has proposed a different pair. I would word the citation around the lattice clock and its 10^-18 realisation, so that the comb (2005) and single-ion control (2012) prizes are not implicitly re-awarded, and so that it follows Kroll's point that the measured achievement, not the idea alone, is what is recognised.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is still novelty and territory. Eriksson and Mehlig see the clock as a refinement of the ruler that the 2005 and 2012 prizes created, and Olsson sees the benefit as still modest. I do not dismiss this: if the committee decides that precision spectroscopy has been honoured enough, B029 falls. There is also a residual attribution tail (Lemonde, Peik and Hollberg on the proposal side; Ludlow, Bloom, Hinkley, Lemke, Kitagawa and the ion-clock groups on the achievement side) that a two-name prize will leave uncredited, and the best ion clocks still compete on accuracy. Finally, the formal redefinition of the second has not happened, and a sceptic can say we are early. I judge these costs lower than the costs on the alternatives: B031 has a credit set and an open many-body mechanism that the condensed-matter members themselves flag, B004 sits next to the 2025 prize with an unresolved four-to-three problem, and B012 and B013 have large-team credit problems.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B031 as prediction followed by decisive experiment, argues the unresolved pairing mechanism belongs in the uncertainties and not in the case against, and rates B029 as a refinement of precision spectroscopy.
responses.response: I accept the distinction you draw: the flat-band picture is stable and the open question is the many-body ground state, and I withdraw any suggestion that the mechanism alone disqualifies the discovery. My remaining concern is narrower and about the credit and reproducibility, which you yourself name. The chair's question was whether superconductivity has been seen in enough independent samples and groups given twist-angle disorder, and your answer was to put that to the experimentalists. As an experimentalist I read that as: reproduced, yes, but with strong sample dependence. Together with Cao, Fatemi and Dean being outside the trio, that is why I rank B031 as my first alternative and not as my preference. On your point that the clock is only a refinement, I would say a magic-wavelength lattice reaching 10^-18 was not available from either the 2005 or 2012 prize work; it is a new route past the quantum-projection-noise limit of a single ion. I would still support a B031 prize on the three names if the committee turns to it.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B031 for the transparent analytic mechanism and a falsifiable prediction, but says B029 is the cleaner fallback if the credit set is judged unsound, and calls the clock a refinement of the ruler created by earlier prizes.
responses.response: I value the analytic mechanism argument; a prediction that experiment then confirms is the strongest kind of physics case, and I agree it is the best theory-experiment story on the shortlist. We are close on one important thing: you say B029 is the cleaner fallback if the credit is unsound, and you have yourself identified that the credit is crowded (earlier continuum theory, Cao and Fatemi, Dean, Yazdani, Young, Efetov). I think that is a weakness in B031 that the committee cannot fix with a wording change. On the refinement claim, the comb is the ruler and the clock is a different instrument built on it; I would not call a measurement advance a lesser discovery if it opens a quantity (fractional frequency at 10^-18, with millimetre redshift resolution) that nobody could observe before. I do take your point that cleaner credit alone should not decide the matter, and I do not rest on it.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B029 but asks whether to wait for the redefinition of the second, and wants the citation written around the measured achievement and not around the idea alone.
responses.response: I agree on the citation and have changed my wording accordingly: the revised citation names both the magic-wavelength trapping and the realisation at 10^-18 confirmed in independent laboratories. On waiting for the redefinition of the second, I would not make it a condition. The Nobel Prize recognises a discovery or invention, and the evidence here is the cross-laboratory comparisons, which already exist; the redefinition is a metrological decision that depends on further consensus and could be years away. Waiting would also risk the credit set, since the field is large and growing. You and Lindroth are better placed than I am to judge the proposal history and ion-clock competition, and I would like you to confirm directly that they do not change the two names.

responses.point: Olsson ranked B029 last, doubts that it is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes and sees the benefit to humanity as still modest, and prefers NV-centre spin control and sensing (B001).
responses.response: I take the benefit point seriously and have not dismissed it, but I think the better test is the one you apply to B001: has the achievement already left the laboratory? Clock comparisons at 10^-18, relativistic geodesy and constraints on varying constants are demonstrated, not promised. On B001 I still find the discovery boundary harder to draw: single-centre optical detection, coherent control, nuclear-spin registers and the later sensing applications are different achievements, with Hanson, Awschalom and Lukin all having claims, and your own two-name set leaves out a person who is on the ballot. If the committee wanted a sensing prize, I would want to see that set justified first. That is the reason B001 is not among my alternatives, though I respect the case and my view is unchanged by the round-one exchange.

responses.point: Danielsson proposes B029 together with B037 (Halzen alone) as a second distinct part, with B012 and B016 as fallbacks, and himself names the sole credit of a collaboration and the unknown origin of most of the flux as problems.
responses.response: I am glad you place B029 in your configuration, and I agree that a second part is permitted. I would not support B037 as a part. A single name for IceCube overlooks the AMANDA precursor, the deep-water and deep-ice pioneers and the collaboration, which you raise yourself, and the source association (TXS 0506+056 at about 3 sigma, Galactic plane recently) is not yet the kind of independently confirmed result I ask for. As a detector builder in astroparticle physics I would like to see neutrino astronomy honoured, but later and with a credit set the record supports. I also have to be careful here: I disclosed that B037 is in my subfield, and I would weigh recusal on it if it became decisive. So I keep a one-part prize.

responses.point: Lindroth prefers B029 with the two names, treats cross-laboratory comparisons at 10^-18 as sufficient for recognition now, and herself flags the unresolved division of credit with ion-clock and comb work.
responses.response: I agree that recognition is timely. As the committee's atomic physicist, please say whether the proposal history (Katori 2001-2003, with Lemonde, Peik and Hollberg) and the ion-clock work change the two names, because I have no independent basis for judging that and the chair's summary asks for it. You also disclosed your close collaboration with the attosecond community; none of those names is on this ballot, so I see no obstacle for B029. I would be happy for the committee to ask for an outside assessment on the credit question before final ranking, though I would not delay the ballot for it.

uncertainties: Whether the proposal history (Lemonde, Peik, Hollberg) and the team contributions to 10^-18 (Ludlow, Bloom, Hinkley, Lemke, Kitagawa and the ion-clock groups) are adequately captured by crediting only Katori and Ye; the atomic physicists must confirm, and I cannot verify priority dates myself.
Whether a majority regards the lattice clock as distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes; this is a judgement about novelty that I cannot settle by evidence.
Whether the condensed-matter judgements on B031 (mechanism, device reproducibility, Cao, Fatemi and Dean) are as I understand them, since I depend on colleagues for them.
I have not checked the timetable for a redefinition of the second, and I treat it as irrelevant to the decision.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Katori, Ye or their groups, so I see no conflict on B029. My own work (Fermi-LAT, PAMELA, XL-Calibur, polarimetry) is adjacent to B013, my second alternative, and to B037 in astroparticle physics, so I would weigh recusal on either if it became decisive. As chair I am one of the four who prefer B029, and I will keep my role as process lead separate from my vote. I also note Johansson's disclosed closeness to B004 and defer to the committee on how he should step back from that candidate.
